title: Bikeshedding time: readable vs. writable symmetry in properties and methods.
body:
So, this is basically blocked on #44. The thing is, I have made various awkward API choices because I wanted to keep writable and readable APIs disjoint. Right now we have:
### As of Now
#### ReadableStream
- `waitForReadable()`
- `readableState`
- `abort(reason)`
- `finished` promise
- `"finished"` state
### WritableStream
- `waitForWritable()`
- `writableState`
- `dispose(reason)`
- `close()`
- `closed` promise
- `"closing"` and `"closed"` state
### If Unified

If we gave up on the idea of being able to have a single object be both a readable and writable stream, i.e. went with `{ in, out }` for _both_ duplex and transform, we could try something like
#### ReadableStream
- `wait()`
- `state`
- `dispose(reason)`
- `closed` promise
- `"closed"` state
#### WritableStream
- `wait()`
- `state`
- `dispose(reason)`
- `close()`
- `closed` promise
- `"closing"` and `"closed"` state
### Your Idea Here?

I'm not married to any of these names. Here are the big questions, using the "meat-grinder" vs. "telephone" analogy from #21.
- Should "meat-grinder" streams use `{ in, out }` or a single object with both readable and writable methods?
  - If you choose this, we need to modify `pipe` to work not only with writable streams, but with these "telephone" streams, by writing to `in` and returning `out`. (Instead of just writing to and returning its writable-stream argument.)
- Should "telephone" streams use `{ in, out }` or a single object with both readable and writable methods?
- Which set of names do you like? You are not allowed to use the short names if you said single-object for either of the previous questions. (But you don't _have_ to use the short names if you choose `{ in, out }` for both)
- Do you have better ideas for names? E.g. "finished" vs. "closed" and "abort" vs. "dispose" seems weird.
